issue: Can a non-retroactive change in § 924(c)'s anti-stacking rule, possibly combined with the Guidelines' unusually-long-sentence provision, be an extraordinary and compelling reason for a sentence reduction under 18 U.S.C. § 3582(c)(1)(A)?

sides.position: The § 924(c) anti-stacking amendment cannot constitute an extraordinary and compelling reason, because doing so would give a non-retroactive change retroactive effect; § 1B1.13(b)(6) cannot change that result.
cases: United States v. Thacker, 4 F.4th 569 (7th Cir. 2021)
United States v. Andrews, 12 F.4th 255 (3d Cir. 2021)
United States v. Rutherford, 120 F.4th 360 (3d Cir. 2024)
United States v. Austin, 125 F.4th 688 (5th Cir. 2025)
United States v. McCall, 56 F.4th 1048 (6th Cir. 2022)
United States v. Crandall, 25 F.4th 582 (8th Cir. 2022)
United States v. Jenkins, 50 F.4th 1185 (D.C. Cir. 2022)
United States v. Black, No. 24-1191 (7th Cir. 2025)

sides.position: The anti-stacking amendment can be an extraordinary and compelling reason under U.S.S.G. § 1B1.13(b)(6), which the Commission validly adopted under 28 U.S.C. § 994(t) to resolve the circuit split.
cases: United States v. Ruvalcaba, 26 F.4th 14 (1st Cir. 2022)
United States v. McCoy, 981 F.3d 271 (4th Cir. 2020)
United States v. Chen, 48 F.4th 1092 (9th Cir. 2022)
United States v. McGee, 992 F.3d 1035 (10th Cir. 2021)

this_court: Cannot constitute an extraordinary and compelling reason; the majority follows Thacker and joins the Third Circuit's Rutherford decision, rejecting the § 1B1.13(b)(6) approach as contrary to the First Step Act's prospective-only choice.
quote: We recognize Thacker’s holding that § 924(c)’s anti-stacking amendment cannot constitute an extraordinary and compelling reason for a sentence reduction is not consensus; the courts of appeals have split on the issue.
cite: United States v. Eural Black, No. 24-1191 (7th Cir. 2025)
